title: empty-path Glob/Grep trusts the working directory without checking it

provenance.found_by: NorthWoods Sentinel Labs (NWS swarm, run by Margin, for Rob Chuvala)
provenance.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029 (NWS execution-boundary review, round 2, against cortex v6.13.0)

finding: Grep with no path or Glob with a bare wildcard produces zero path tokens, and the guard auto-grants, trusting that dispatch set cwd inside allowedDirs. The guard never verifies cwd itself. If cwd can resolve outside allowedDirs (misconfig, race, symlinked cwd), an empty-path Grep searches out of scope.

repros.verbatim: (mechanism, no single-command repro given) — a Grep call with no `path` field, invoked with the hook's process.cwd() outside every allowedDirs/readOnlyDirs entry, is auto-granted without cortex ever resolving or checking cwd against the policy.
repros.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029, finding F6
repros.outcome: Reproduced by this corpus's spawn-hook check: path-guard.hook.ts is spawned with CORTEX_PATH_GUARD scoping allowedDirs to one fixture directory, cwd set (as a spawn option) to a DIFFERENT fixture directory outside that scope, and a Grep call with no `path` field — the hook still emits permissionDecision:allow.

expected: In the empty-token branch (Glob/Grep with no explicit path), the hook should resolve process.cwd() and containment-check it against allowedDirs/readOnlyDirs before granting, instead of unconditionally trusting that dispatch already scoped it correctly.
